newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somali faction accuses Ethiopia of arming rival.
newsitem.headline: Somali faction accuses Ethiopia of arming rival.

text.p: A Somali faction accused Ethiopia on Friday of supplying more than 70 tonnes of weapons and ammunition to a rival faction in violation of a U.N. arms embargo.

Mohamed Kanyare Afrah, interior minister in a self -proclaimed government led by Hussein Aideed, said the munitions which arrived in northern Mogadishu on Wednesday were brought by trucks overland from an Ethiopian military base at Shilabo.

He accused Ethiopia of violating an arms embargo on Somalia imposed by the U.N. Security Council in 1992 by arming north Mogadishu faction leader Ali Mahdi Mohamed, who has close links to Addis Ababa.
The arms and ammunition were unloaded from trucks at a depot guarded by dozens of "technical" battlewagons in northern Mogadishu in broad daylight on Wednesday watched by hundreds of people.
An Ali Mahdi spokesman said the accusation that Ethiopia's government was involved in the arms shipment was baseless.

He said businessmen had long smuggled weapons and ammunition into Somalia and Ali Mahdi was free to buy weapons from such dealers. He said no other country, including Ethiopia, supplied his munitions.

More than 130 people were killed and 1,500 wounded in a week of fierce battles between Aideed and Ali Mahdi's militiamen and their allies in December. Some residents said both sides only stopped fighting because they had run short of ammunition.
Ali Mahdi, who like rival south Mogadishu leader Aideed is a self-styled president of Somalia, has been in Ethiopia since mid -December for what Ethiopian officials say are Somali peace talks.

Somali Moslem fundamentalists have called for a "jihad" or holy war against Ethiopian forces which thrust into southwest Somalia last month. Ethiopia said it beat back Somali Moslem fundamentalists attacking Dollo town, straddling the border.
